newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: SOCCER-HIGUITA RESUMES TRAINING WITH FORMER CLUB.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HIGUITA RESUMES TRAINING WITH FORMER CLUB.

text.p: Eccentric Colombian goalkeeper Rene Higuita took part in a training session on Wednesday with his former club Atletico Nacional, but it was not clear whether he would resume his career.
Higuita, 30, turned up at the club in Medellin, Colombia's second city, just over two weeks after his home in a northwestern suburb of the city was bombed by unidentified attackers.
Police said the intruders forced their way past a maid and detonated dynamite, which damaged windows, doors and furniture but caused no injuries.

Coach Juan Jose Pelez refused to confirm that Higuita, who quit in November for "personal reasons", was making a comeback. "He wants to return but he has his own struggle," said Pelez without elaborating.
"Rene's arrival always generates happiness. The players and the coaching staff welcomed him with open arms."

The club's goalkeeping coach said if Higuita was thinking of returning, it would be several weeks before he could begin playing. "He's overweight. He has to get in shape and it will be a question of weeks," said Pedro Antonio Zape.
Higuita is best known for his unorthodox approach to the art of goalkeeping, symoblised by the remarkable "scorpion" save he made for Colombia in a friendly against England at Wembley.
Instead of simply catching the ball, Higuita threw himself forward and kicked it away with his heels.
